sources.note: Custom OpenAI-compatible provider: createOpenAICompatible with apiKey/apiHost, the chat URL is forced to `${apiHost}${apiPath}` by a custom fetch, listModels uses fetchRemoteModels; temperature/topP/maxOutputTokens/stream come from settings.
normalizeOpenAIApiHostAndPath: trims, strips trailing slash, prepends https:// when no scheme, default apiPath '/chat/completions'; accepts a host that already ends with /chat/completions.
fetchRemoteModels: GET {apiHost}/models with Authorization: Bearer; throws if json.data is missing; maps id, optional name/context_length/architecture.

buildHeaders sets Content-Type: application/json on every request (also GET); with useProxy on web the call is rerouted to https://cors-proxy.chatboxai.app/proxy-api/completions with CHATBOX-TARGET-URI; otherwise plain fetch() from the renderer.
stream !== false means streaming; stream === false wraps the model with simulateStreaming (non-stream request).
streamText(...) with allowSystemInMessages, tools, maxRetries 0; temperature/topP/maxOutputTokens come from callSettings.
Chatbox closes the stream at the exact event `data: [DONE]` (terminate) so a gateway that keeps the connection open without [DONE] is not detected as finished; non-JSON frames pass through.

L173-L325 getArgs (keys: model, user, max_tokens, temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, response_format, stop, seed, provider-option extras, reasoning_effort, verbosity, messages, tools, tool_choice); L331-L353 doGenerate (no stream key); L427-L440 doStream (stream:true, stream_options only when includeUsage); L835-L916 response/chunk zod schemas.

L33-L45 user content: single text part becomes a string, otherwise an array (text/image_url/video_url/input_audio/file parts); L224-L255 assistant: content = text or null when tool calls exist and no text, tool_calls with JSON-string arguments; tool messages {role:'tool', tool_call_id, content:string}.
L146-L152: Authorization: Bearer <apiKey> + User-Agent suffix `ai-sdk/openai-compatible/<version>`; includeUsage option (not set by Chatbox).
nameConversation: the auto-title request is one user message ('Based on the chat history, give this conversation a name...').
Title generation calls the same model.chat(...) path (streaming by default, same temperature/topP settings), reads text parts.

setup.baseUrl: Provider > API Host: http://<gateway-host>:8787/v1  (WITH /v1; the client then POSTs to `${apiHost}${apiPath}` with the default API Path /chat/completions and lists models at `${apiHost}/models`). A host typed without http:// gets https:// prepended.
setup.model: Add the agent name (e.g. agent/sample) as a model of the custom provider, or use the provider's model-fetch button which calls GET /v1/models; the selected model id is sent as 'model'.
setup.apiKey: Provider > API Key (sent as Authorization: Bearer). Provider type: Settings > Model Provider > Add custom provider > API mode 'OpenAI API Compatible' (field names in code: apiHost, apiPath, apiKey; Improve Network Compatibility = useProxy).
setup.notes: Where requests originate depends on the platform: mobile uses a native request path; desktop and web run fetch() inside the renderer (browser context), so CORS applies unless the 'useProxy' (Improve Network Compatibility) switch is on. On web with useProxy and a non-localhost host the call is relayed through Chatbox's own cors-proxy.chatboxai.app server (the gateway then sees Chatbox's cloud IP and the body travels via a third party). On desktop with useProxy the request goes through desktopDirectRequestFromWindow. For a self-hosted gateway reached from the web version, allow CORS (preflight below) or use the desktop app.

cases.title: Model list fetch (custom provider 'fetch models')

evidence.note: Only Authorization is set by the model code; Content-Type: application/json is added by buildHeaders for every request (request.ts#L45-L47). User-Agent behaviour of the platform fetch is not specified.

cases.notes: Throws (ApiError with the raw JSON) if the response has no data key; data items need id, optional name (becomes nickname), context_length, architecture. object/created/owned_by are typed but not used. If the list call fails the UI shows an error and the user can still add models manually.

cases.title: Streaming chat, default settings (no stream_options, no sampling keys)

evidence.note: doStream sets stream:true and stream_options only if config.includeUsage, which custom-openai.ts does not set. temperature/top_p/max_tokens are undefined unless the session sets them. User-Agent value is from provider-utils withUserAgentSuffix (exact runtime suffix not verified).

cases.notes: A new session usually starts with a system message (default system prompt) so messages may be [system, user]; role is 'system' (never 'developer'). Every chunk is validated against a zod schema in which `choices` is a REQUIRED array: a chunk without choices (e.g. a bare usage chunk) is turned into an error part; delta.role must be 'assistant' or '' if present; unknown extra fields are allowed. Chatbox force-terminates the stream at `data: [DONE]`; without [DONE] it relies on the body ending. SSE content-type is not validated.

cases.title: Streaming chat with every optional setting Chatbox exposes (temperature, top_p, max tokens)

evidence.note: getCallSettings returns only temperature, topP, maxOutputTokens (and reasoning providerOptions). frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, stop, seed, user, n, logit_bias are never sent by this provider.

cases.notes: max_tokens (not max_completion_tokens) is the key name; a non-integer or <1 value is dropped client-side. Kimi K2/K3 ids have temperature/top_p dropped.

cases.title: Non-streaming chat (provider setting stream = false): note there is NO stream key at all

evidence.note: doGenerate posts getArgs() output unchanged; the stream key is only added by doStream. Chatbox then replays the result as a simulated stream.

cases.notes: Response schema: choices is a required array of {message:{role?: 'assistant', content: string|null|array, tool_calls?}, finish_reason?}; id/created/model/usage are nullish. message.role, if present, must be exactly 'assistant'.

cases.title: Automatic conversation naming (same chat path, one user message)

evidence.note: model.chat(toModelMessages(nameConversation(...))) with only {sessionId}; streaming and sampling settings are the session's, so stream:true by default. The text template is from src/shared/prompts.ts#L4-L35.

messages.content:
Based on the chat history, give this conversation a name.
Keep it short - 10 words max, no quotes.
Use English.
Just provide the name, nothing else.

Here's the conversation:

```
Hello

---------

Hi there
```

Name this conversation in 10 words or less.
Use English.
Only give the name, nothing else.

The name is:

cases.notes: A second agent run is triggered after the first assistant reply (unless 'auto generate title' is off). If the naming model/provider is configured in settings (threadNamingModel) it may be another provider. There is no dedicated connectivity-test request: the provider 'check' is the models-list call.

cases.title: System prompt (role system, string content; developer never sent)

evidence.note: case 'system' pushes {role:'system', content}. Chatbox passes allowSystemInMessages:true so a system message may also appear mid-history.

cases.notes: Plain string content everywhere for text-only turns; no name fields.

cases.title: User turn made of several text parts (content as array of text parts)

evidence.note: Converter verified: a user message with more than one part (or a single non-text part) becomes an array of {type:'text', text} / image_url parts; Chatbox producing multiple text parts (e.g. text file attachments inlined next to the prompt) is assumed, not traced.

content.text:
File: notes.txt
Buy milk
Call Bob

cases.notes: The gateway must accept content as either a string or an array of {type:'text'} parts.

cases.title: User message with an attached image (image_url data URL)

evidence.note: image file parts become {type:'image_url', image_url:{url:'data:<mime>;base64,...'}} (or the remote URL for url data). Audio becomes input_audio, PDF becomes a file part, video becomes video_url.

cases.notes: Image input (docs/images.md): the data-URL image is decoded, checked and stored as an input file of the caller, and reaches an image-capable agent (the lab fixture agent declares image input) in its provider's own image shape. A text-only agent answers 400 unsupported_content with error.param on this part instead.

cases.title: Follow-up turn after a tool call (assistant content null + tool_calls, then tool message)

evidence.note: assistant: content = toolCalls.length > 0 ? text || null : text, so null when the model produced only tool calls; arguments = JSON.stringify(input); tool message content is a string (JSON.stringify for json outputs).

messages.content: What is the weather in Paris?

function.name: get_weather
function.description: Get the weather for a city

cases.notes: If the assistant also produced text before calling tools, content is that text string. Reasoning replays add reasoning_content on assistant messages when the earlier turn returned reasoning.

cases.title: Request with tools (MCP/built-in tools enabled); tool_choice and parallel_tool_calls not sent

evidence.note: tools mapped to {type:'function', function:{name, description, parameters, strict?}}; tool_choice is undefined unless the caller passes toolChoice (Chatbox's streamText call does not). parallel_tool_calls is not part of this provider's body at all.

messages.content: What is the weather in Paris?

function.name: get_weather
function.description: Get the weather for a city

cases.notes: Default chats have no tools key; it appears only when tools (MCP servers, web search, knowledge base, etc.) are active. Streamed tool_call deltas are tolerated with missing index or with the name arriving late.

cases.title: Reasoning effort chosen for a reasoning-capable model id

evidence.note: reasoning_effort: compatibleOptions.reasoningEffort ?? custom reasoning level is a top-level body key (verified). Chatbox strips stale reasoning options for model ids it does not recognise as reasoning-capable (abstract-ai-sdk.ts#L253-L280), so for an arbitrary agent name it is normally absent; not tested end to end.

cases.notes: Responses may include delta.reasoning_content or delta.reasoning, rendered as thinking; <think>...</think> tags in content are also extracted by extractReasoningMiddleware.

cases.title: Browser preflight for GET /v1/models (web version / desktop renderer without useProxy)

evidence.note: Plain fetch() from the renderer with Authorization + Content-Type: application/json (non-simple headers) forces a preflight. The origin of the hosted web app is assumed to be https://web.chatboxai.app; the desktop app's origin differs.

cases.notes: A 204 is equally acceptable. Without a correct preflight answer the web version shows a network error even though curl works.

cases.title: Browser preflight for POST /v1/chat/completions (web version / desktop renderer without useProxy)

evidence.note: authorization and content-type are certain; the AI SDK also sets a user-agent request header which Chromium-based browsers may keep and then list in Access-Control-Request-Headers (not verified).

cases.notes: Best practice: echo back whatever Access-Control-Request-Headers asks for. The streamed response must also carry Access-Control-Allow-Origin.
